Forwarding the customer targets. I'm blocking time this week to finalize the test harness. High-level engineering test spec below — will deliver an executable script and CSV of results by 11/10.

ENGINEERING TEST SPEC (summary):
1) Workloads / prompt-size distribution:
   - Profile A: short prompts (<= 1k tokens) — 40%
   - Profile B: medium prompts (4k tokens) — 30%
   - Profile C: long prompts (32k tokens) — 25%
   - Profile D: extreme (64k tokens, sparsely used) — 5%
2) Test types:
   - Baseline latency: per-request p50/p95/p99, TTFT (cold vs warmed KV cache)
   - Throughput: tokens/sec and completed requests/sec at steady-state under fixed concurrency (1,4,8,16)
   - Concurrency ramp: 1 -> 16 streams, record latency and token throughput
   - KV cache impact: benchmark hit vs miss paths (warm prefix caching; measured hit-rate sweep 0->100%)
   - Memory/CPU/GPU telemetry to correlate regressions
3) Environment & variants:
   - Hosted Redwood default runtime (v2.4) — default kernel selection
   - Quantized weights variant (int8) to test cost/throughput tradeoffs
4) Success metrics (confirming customer's ask but clarifying):
   - For Profile B (4k): p95 <= 200ms; TTFT < 150ms on warmed path
   - For Profile C (32k): p95 <= 900ms; throughput >= 10 tokens/sec per stream at 8-token generation step size
   - Concurrency: maintain p95 targets at 16 concurrent streams for mixed profile distribution
5) Artifacts produced:
   - benchmark_results_20261110.csv (CSV with per-run metrics)
   - kv_cache_test_logs.tar.gz (traces for KV hit/miss experiments)
   - redwood_longcontext-smoke.pdf (executive summary with charts)

Schedule:
- 11/01: Acquire sample prompts and auth for test endpoints from Acme
- 11/02-11/04: Baseline runs (4k/8k) and initial tuning (batching/compilation knobs)
- 11/05-11/09: Long-window and concurrency stress (32k/64k); KV cache sweep
- 11/10: Collate results, produce CSV + PDF executive summary; share with Priyom + Acme

I'll use the Redwood internal harness (wrk-like runner) and make the harness repo available; Karthik will review the test config and validate SLO calculations.

- Aisha
Director, Inference Engineering

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Results: context-stress benchmarking + next steps (MAP update)

Sam / Ellie — attaching the results from our runs (benchmark_results_20261110.csv, kv_cache_test_logs.tar.gz, redwood_longcontext-smoke.pdf). Summary of highlights and how they map to your success criteria: 

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY (short):
- Baseline (4k window) — p95 latency: 165ms; TTFT (warmed KV) 95ms; throughput ~320 tokens/sec per GPU at steady state.
- Medium (8k window) — p95 latency: 320ms; TTFT (warmed) 130ms; stable at 8 concurrent streams.
- Long (32k window) — p95 latency: 780ms; TTFT (warmed) 190ms; throughput ~12 tokens/sec per stream with chunked decoding step=8.
- Extreme (64k window) — p95 latency: 1.6s under identical config; saw increased eviction counts when cache hit-rate < 70% (see logs).
- KV cache impact: with a warmed prefix hit-rate > 85% we observed ~35-45% reduction in p95 for long-window profiles compared to cold runs.
- Concurrency: at 16 concurrent mixed-profile streams p95 tail for long-profile widened to ~980ms; we recommend modest autoscale headroom for production (reserve 20% capacity).

Interpretation vs Acme targets:
- We meet the 8k p95 <= 400ms and 32k p95 <= 900ms targets in warmed-cache steady-state scenarios (as requested).
- TTFT for warmed paths is under the 200ms target for all tested profiles; cold-path TTFT is higher (see CSV).

Next steps / MAP updates:
- 11/12: Review call to walk the PDF and CSV (I've scheduled 11/12 13:00 PT) — invite sent
- 11/13-11/16: Prod onboarding checklist and security questionnaire (Marissa to lead)
- 11/17-11/19: Contract finalization and DocuSign prep
- 11/20: Target signature

Please let me know any follow-ups or if you want additional runs (e.g., different chunking strategies or int8 quantization sweep). If legal is good with the commercial terms we'll start procurement actions today.

Best,
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
